story.title: A version bump that names its rule
story.lede: A new version command recommends the next semantic version from a commit range and names the rule and the commits behind it.

paragraphs.label: Today
paragraphs.text: The tool groups and renders release notes but says nothing about the next version number.

paragraphs.label: Why
paragraphs.text: A bump is only reviewable if it names its rule and the commits that triggered it, and every input commit stays accounted for.

paragraphs.label: What
paragraphs.text: Four rules in a fixed order: breaking, feature, fix, none. A breaking change in a 0.x version bumps the minor part, not the major one, under its own rule id. Entries that match a lower rule are counted, not listed as triggers.

paragraphs.label: How
paragraphs.text: A pure function over the grouped release sections, plus a CLI command that prints the recommendation as JSON.

contributions.adds: Adds the recommender, its CLI command and tests; the second commit pins trigger order and amends the ticket after a review finding.

assets.title: T-005 acceptance criteria at the PR head

story.title: One pure function behind one command
story.lede: The command reads a log stream, groups it with the existing grouper and passes the groups to the recommender.
story.skip: Only one in-process call chain changes: parse, group, recommend, print. No service, store or external boundary is crossed.

answers.q: What does the version command answer?
answers.a: Given the current version and a commit range, it prints the next version, the rule that decided it and the commits that triggered that rule.

answers.q: What happens to a breaking change before 1.0?
answers.a: In a 0.x version a breaking change raises the minor part, under its own rule id, as the ticket asks. A plain feature in the same range is counted, not listed as a trigger.
Yes. Each entry is either a trigger or counted as not triggering; merge commits are counted as ignored.

story.title: Breaking changes before 1.0
story.lede: In a 0.x version a breaking change and a plain feature both raise the minor part, but only the breaking commit is named as the reason.
story.ask: Is it right that, in a 0.x range with a breaking commit and a feature, the feature is counted as not triggering although it alone would give the same next version?
options: Accept: the rule that wins is the reason, as the ticket says
Request a change: list every entry that would give the same bump

layers.summary: Breaking is checked first; inside it, major 0 picks breaking-pre-1.0 and a minor bump. Only the winning rule's entries become triggers.

decisions.text: A breaking change in a 0.x version bumps minor under rule breaking-pre-1.0; a feature in the same range is not a trigger
decisions.plan: Issue 15 criterion 3: when the current major is 0 the bump is minor and the rule id is breaking-pre-1.0. Criterion 4: entries that match a lower rule are not triggers.
decisions.why: Two different rules give the same next version in 0.x, but the output names only the breaking commit. A reader could expect the feature too.
decisions.notice: In the JSON, the feature commit appears only in counts.notTriggering, not in triggers.

q-UBayouski-tracenotes-16-06d9643f-3950-.why: The order did differ from the first ticket text; the human chose section order on Day 7 and amended the ticket. Not the decision investigated here.
